statement: Combined FY2027 capex of the 5 largest AI/cloud spenders >= 1.2x FY2026 (securities filings; on FY2027 filings)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable until FY2027 filings; 2025 sets the trajectory. Four largest Bloc A spenders guided ~$320B for 2025 in February and kept raising (to ~$380B by October); quarterly purchases of P&E rose every quarter ($71.9B Q1 -> $88.2B Q2 -> $97.3B Q3). By end-October all four said 2026 capex would be 'significantly' or 'notably' larger. Year-on-year growth ran ~60-75%, far above the 1.2x bar; the question for resolution is whether growth persists into 2027. Q4 2025 figures were published only in 2026 and are excluded under the as-of rule.

items.summary: A Bloc A frontier developer and partners announced a joint venture to invest up to $500B in AI data centres over four years ($100B initially), alongside the head of government.
items.detail: Stargate (OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, MGX), announced at the White House 2025-01-21. Not a filing; announced intent. Not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: After Q4 2024 earnings, the four largest Bloc A cloud/platform spenders guided up to ~$320B combined capex for 2025, vs ~$230B in 2024 (~+40%), despite a Bloc B low-cost model release prompting efficiency questions.
items.detail: CNBC 2025-02-08: Amazon >$100B, Microsoft $80B (FY2025), Alphabet $75B, Meta $60-65B. NYT 2025-02-08 'What DeepSeek? Big Tech keeps its A.I. building boom alive'.

items.summary: Q1 2025 combined purchases of property and equipment of the four largest spenders: ~$71.9B, roughly flat vs Q4 2024 but +62% year on year.
items.detail: Microsoft 16.7 (FY25Q3), Alphabet 17.2, Amazon 25.0, Meta 12.9 ($B), from 10-Q cash-flow statements (compiled by ai-industry-reviews.com / coolpowerindex.com from SEC XBRL). Filing dates late Apr-early May 2025 (approximate).

items.summary: Q2 2025 combined purchases of P&E of the four: ~$88.2B (+67% y/y); one firm raised full-year guidance to ~$85B.
items.detail: Microsoft 17.1, Alphabet 22.4, Amazon 32.2, Meta 16.5 ($B). Alphabet raised 2025 guidance from $75B to $85B in July. Same compiled SEC-filing source; dates approximate.

items.summary: Q3 2025 combined purchases of P&E of the four: ~$97.3B (+65% y/y). Full-year 2025 guidance raised again: one firm to $91-93B, another to $70-72B, a third to ~$125B; combined ~$380B for 2025.
items.detail: Microsoft 19.4 (FY26Q1; ~$35B incl. finance leases), Alphabet 24.0, Amazon 35.1, Meta 18.8 ($B). Reuters 2025-10-29 (Alphabet, Meta), Livemint/CNBC 2025-10-31.

items.summary: All four largest spenders signalled higher 2026 capex: 'significant increase' (one CFO), growth 'considerably faster' in 2026 (another), capex growth to accelerate in the new fiscal year (a third), and 'higher next year' (the fourth). Analysts projected ~$3T of big-tech data-centre spending through 2028.
items.detail: Q3 2025 calls: Alphabet CFO Ashkenazi, Meta (Zuckerberg: 'aggressively front-load building capacity'), Microsoft CFO Hood, Amazon CFO Olsavsky. Morgan Stanley ~$3T 2025-2028 estimate cited by Livemint.

items.summary: Identity of the fifth-largest spender and capex definitions differ by firm (cash P&E vs including finance leases; fiscal years ending June or May). The indicator needs a fixed list and definition before FY2027 resolution.
items.detail: Candidates for fifth: Oracle (FY ends May), CoreWeave, xAI (private), ByteDance/Alibaba (Bloc B, different exchanges). Microsoft reports finance leases separately.
